An alternative-media report (26 June 2025): an 18-year-old trans woman was found dead with signs of physical assault in a river after being reported missing the previous day; her mother reported the disappearance to local police; the chairperson of a national LGBT alliance called the killing part of a pattern of violence against trans women and renewed calls for the equality bill. The case is in a different region — national-climate evidence.

A national legal rights overview page frames what a visitor to this division stands under: no general national anti-discrimination law (only piecemeal local ordinances), transgender people may not change their legal gender, same-sex marriage is not recognized (the family code confines marriage to 'a man and a woman'), and the equality bill remains pending in the national legislature. Citing a regional news outlet (24 June 2019), the page notes that only 4 local government units across the wider region had passed pro-LGBT ordinances by mid-2019, consistent with the record's caution that the absence of a regional signal reflects sparse documentation rather than confirmed absence of divergence.

rewrites.blindSummary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 0.48% (regional case table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year.

There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression. Protective national framework (the gender identity law in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, the anti-discrimination law) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (the gender-identity support programme excluded from the 2026 budget; a health-ministry circular restricting that programme for minors; a pending legislative initiative) and administrative document friction from civil-registry identification-system issuance failures (a comptroller final report 2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.
rewrites.blindTangential: National frame applies: the reporting organisation records LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases rising in this region during 2025 alongside the national increase; a recorded-case rise is adjacent to trans risk via general hostility but is not a visitor-specific exposure.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: Resident-facing: the gender identity law's name/sex rectification (over twelve thousand people by December 2025; only 15.7% of adults who declared trans/non-binary in the 2024 census; the nonbinary X marker still requires a judicial process) and the gender-identity support programme removed from the 2026 budget affect residents, not visitors.
blindSourceSummaries: A country dossier (published March 2026) contains no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding, which is the basis for this record's national-score assessment: same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; the hate-crime law has covered sexual orientation and gender identity since 2012; legal gender recognition by self-determination since 2019; a third sex option on birth certificates since 2006; and the 2025-26 rollback in which the national legislature excluded the gender-identity support programme from the 2026 budget bill, an action condemned by civil society groups and the national ombuds for children. The dossier itself carries no division-specific information.

The 24th annual report by a case-counting organisation (published March 2026) supplies this record's division-specific figures from its national regional table: this division is placed at 0.65% of nationally documented abuse cases, with a +25% year-on-year rise, a share-based reading that the report warns reflects weaker local safety rather than low risk. Nationally, the report records a record 3,620 cases and complaints of discrimination in 2025 (+27.1%, the highest in 24 years), with only two regions falling (one by 17.56%, the other by 14.35%) while the other 14 regions rose; it reads the shift as hatred expanding into regions with less public debate, which is what this record's mid-share reading rests on. The 2024 share cited in this record's comparison is not reproduced in this 2025 edition.
